title: The banjo introduction dubbed on afterward
summary: Louis disliked the take, so a banjoist brought in at Trummy's suggestion devised the introduction, dubbed in after the record was made.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: they thought was really going to go was, 'You've Got A Lot Of Living To Do.' We made two sides. When we made the record, we had one little lead sheet that Louis played; it was written for Louis. And Billy Kyle scribbled a couple of little rhythm patterns. That's the only music we had. And we made it, and we listened to it and listened to it and listened to it -- and Louis wasn't satisfied with it. He says, 'I don't like that. Can't something just be done with this record to kind of pep it up a little or do something...?' And one of us, I think Trummy said, 'I know a banjo player (he had a directory) that lives close to here, I believe, and maybe if we got that banjo and made an introduction...' I don't know why he thought of that...
Yes. I think it was Trummy. So we brought that banjo player there, and we fiddled around...

His name was Tony something. I've got it written down, but I couldn't remember the last name. He says, 'Let me try this introduction.' And he took his banjo, after trying a lot of things: [SINGS REFRAIN OF Hello Dolly INTRODUCTION], and he laid it down like that. You know the introduction to the song. So they dubbed it in.
Oh, after the record they put this...
After the record was made! But I think he continued to make the rest of the record...
I haven't heard in so long...
I haven't listened to it really that close. But I know Louis didn't care a damn thing about it. He didn't care.
